conversation.Statement: Good afternoon, this is Brian Matthews from the IRS Tax Refund Department. Am I speaking with Jamie Evans?
Yes, this is Jamie. Is everything okay?
Actually, Jamie, I'm calling with good news. Our records show that you qualify for a federal tax refund adjustment under the recent stimulus revisions. We are processing your case now.
Wait, seriously? I thought I already filed my taxes. I barely had time to get those done.

That's correct, but the IRS recently enacted a retroactive provision for working parents, and you are eligible for an additional $3,500 refund. To initiate the release, we need to verify your identity and process a clearance fee, per federal regulations.
A clearance fee? I haven't heard of that before. Is that normal?

Under Section 27A, all refund adjustments over $2,000 require a one-time identity verification fee, which is fully refundable. The IRS cannot release funds without this step. The deadline for this cycle is today at 3 p.m.
I have a work meeting soon and need to pick up my daughter. Can I just handle this online?
Unfortunately, online processing has temporarily been suspended for these cases. To prevent forfeiture of your $3,500 refund, I urge you to complete the verification now.
How much is the fee, and how do I pay it?

The federal clearance fee for your refund bracket is $298. It must be paid via certified method, such as a prepaid Visa or Mastercard gift card, or by direct transfer through Zelle. Which method is most convenient for you?
Um, probably the gift card. I guess I could run to the store.

Excellent. Please purchase a $300 Visa or Mastercard gift card. Once you have it, call me back at this direct IRS processing number. Do not share the card with anyone else, to protect your personal data.
Okay, but can I wait until after I pick up my daughter from school?

I must remind you, Jamie, if you miss today's 3 p.m. IRS deadline, your refund will be placed on indefinite hold, and you may become ineligible for this adjustment. I'd strongly advise acting immediately.
Wow, that's a lot of money to lose. Alright, I'll try to get it done now.
Thank you. Please stay on the line while you purchase the card, or call me back as soon as you have it. Delays may result in the IRS escalating your file for non-compliance.
Okay, I'm heading to the store now.

Once you have the gift card, scratch off the back and read the numbers to me. After verification, your $3,500 refund will be released to your account within 24 hours. Please confirm when you're ready.
Alright, give me a few minutes.
Remember, Jamie, failure to complete this process can result in your refund being withheld and may signal a mismatch in your tax records. That could lead to further IRS review or fines.
Okay, I have the card now. I'll read you the numbers.
Please read each set of numbers slowly and clearly so I can verify your payment and update the IRS system.
The number is 5432 9876 1234 5678, expiration 08/27, code 456.
Thank you. I'll process this right away. You should see your refund reflected in your bank account soon. If there are any issues, I will call you back for additional verification.
